87.h: 83 - al-Nuʿmān ibn Muqarrin Abū ʿAmr al-Muzanī *
87.t:
He is: al-Nuʿmān ibn ʿAmr ibn Muqarrin ibn ʿĀʾidh ibn Mīja (1) ibn Hujayr ibn Naṣr ibn Ḥubshiyyah ibn Kaʿb ibn Thawr ibn Hudhmah ibn Lāṭim ibn ʿUthmān ibn Muzaynah.
Abū ʿAmr al-Muzanī, the commander.
His first battle was al-Aḥzāb, and he was present at the Pledge of al-Riḍwān. He settled in Kufa and governed Kaskar for ʿUmar, then dismissed him, then sent him in command of the Muslims on the day of the battle of Nihāwand, and on that day he was the first to be martyred.
أخبرنا سنقر الحلبي بها، أنبأنا عبد اللطيف اللغوي، أنبأنا عبد الحق اليوسفي، أنبأنا علي بن محمد، أنبأنا أبو الحسن الحمامي، أنبأنا ابن قانع، حدثنا الحسن بن علي بن كامل، حدثنا عفان (2) ، حدثنا حماد، عن أبي عمران الجوني، عن علقمة بن عبد الله المزني، عن معقل بن يسار، عن النعمان بن مقرن، أنه قال:
I was present with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when, if he had not fought in the early part of the day, he would wait until the sun had passed its zenith (3) .
Al-Tirmidhī declared it authentic (الصحيح).
A similar report was narrated from: ⟦1:403⟧
زياد (1) بن جبير، عن أبيه، عن النعمان.
Shuʿbah: Iyās ibn Muʿāwiyah informed me, saying: Ibn al-Musayyib said to me: Where are you from?
I said: From Muzaynah.
He said: I remember the day ʿUmar announced the death of al-Nuʿmān ibn Muqarrin from the pulpit.
Al-Wāqidī said: Nihāwand took place in the year 21.
I say: Saʿīd memorised that, and he was seven years old.
Al-Nuʿmān had brothers: Suwayd Abū ʿAdī; Sinān, who was among those present at the Trench; Maʿqil, the father of ʿAbd Allāh the hadith scholar (المحدث); ʿAqīl Abū Ḥakīm; and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān.
It was narrated from Mujāhid that he said: The weepers were the sons of Muqarrin, seven in number.
Al-Wāqidī said: I heard that they were present at the Trench.
It is also said: al-Nuʿmān's patronymic (الكنية) was Abū Ḥakīm, and he held the banner of Muzaynah on the day of the Conquest.
Narrating from him: ولده معاوية، ومسلم بن هيصم، وجماعة.
Ibn Isḥāq said: He was killed while he was the commander of the people, in the year 21.
Shuʿbah: from ʿAlī ibn Zayd, from Abū ʿUthmān, who said:
I came to ʿUmar with the news of the death of al-Nuʿmān ibn Muqarrin, and he put his hand on his face and wept. ⟦1:404⟧
Abū ʿImrān al-Jawnī: from ʿAlqamah ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Muzanī, from Maʿqil ibn Yasār:
That ʿUmar consulted al-Hurmuzān about: Isfahan, Fars, and Azerbaijan.
He said: Isfahan is the head, and Fars and Azerbaijan are the two wings. If you cut off one wing, the head and the other wing recover (1) , but if you cut off the head, both wings fall.
Then ʿUmar said to al-Nuʿmān ibn Muqarrin: I am going to appoint you.
He said: As a tax collector, no; as a raider, yes.
He said: Then you are a raider.
So he dispatched him and sent word to the people of Kufa to reinforce him, and among them were: Ḥudhayfah, al-Zubayr, al-Mughīrah, al-Ashʿath, and ʿAmr ibn Maʿdī Karib.
He then related the hadith at length, and it is in the (Mustadrak of al-Ḥākim).
And in it: He said: O Allah, grant al-Nuʿmān martyrdom through the victory of the Muslims, and grant them conquest.
They said Amen, and he waved his banner three times, then charged, and he was the first to fall (may Allah be pleased with him).
Dhū al-Ḥājibayn fell from his grey mule, and his belly was split open, and Allah granted the conquest. Then I came to al-Nuʿmān while he had a breath of life left, and I brought him water and poured it over his face to wash off the dust.
He said: Who is this?
I said: Maʿqil.
He said: What has become of the people?
I said: Allah has granted the conquest.
He said: Praise be to Allah. Write to ʿUmar about this.
Then his soul departed (may Allah be pleased with him) (2) . ⟦1:405⟧
